verbatims.quote: Kill B and A before an app reviewer or a state regulator kills them for you. 'Beat the books' reads as a promise of winnings, and every responsible marketing code I work under says don't imply that.
A line move at our shop isn't 'money moving.' Half the time it's us shading after one sharp limit bet or copying a market maker. F oversells what an open-versus-now chart actually shows.
A screen that refreshes three times a day is a history book, not an edge. I'd never pay for it, and 'Get an edge on the books' gets laughed out of any sharp Discord.
Four books, a few pulls a day. The first time a user taps a price that's already gone, that's the delete. Timestamp every number or don't show it.
A wins the click, no question. Rec bettors want to feel like they're getting one over on the book. Just know some operator partners won't run creative that says it.
The insider directory is the sneaky good part. My audience already follows five guys on X. Putting them in one place next to the odds is actually useful.
Put My Teams first. That's what brings people back on a Tuesday in October. Line moves matter to maybe one user in ten.
Hot streaks on the home screen is a gambler's fallacy machine. Lead with that and expect pushback from RG advocates, whatever the headline says.

researcher_note: stale_or_wrong_odds (188) beat guaranteed_win_claims (179). B backfires worst: 149/250 flagged. A wins media and affiliates on appeal but carries 110 flags. F leads overall though traders call 'money's moving' misleading (no handle data).
